segments.narration: Two unlicensed treasure hunters dug up a Bronze Age sky map. A bronze plate thirty centimetres wide, studded with gold stars.
They had no permit, so they sold it the next day for thirty-one thousand marks. It disappeared into the black market and kept changing hands.
Think about what was being passed around. Something made thirty-six hundred years ago, traded by dealers who could not read a mark on it.
In 2002 a state archaeologist posed as a buyer in a Basel hotel. Police took the disc back. The sellers had wanted seven hundred thousand marks for it.
Then the scientists read it. Seven dots are the Pleiades, and the gold arcs on the rim mark exactly where the sun sets at the solstices.
